title: Aurion Industries — Onprem / Air-gapped discovery
summary: Discovery call for on-prem, air-gapped deployment requirements. Aurion is a regulated manufacturing firm evaluating Redwood Private for sensitive IP and PII. Key concerns: fully offline updates, hardware constraints, KMS/HSM integration, SOC2/ISO compliance, maintenance model, and pilot timelines. Agreed next steps: share security pack, architecture diagram for air-gapped installer, hardware spec sheet, schedule on-site feasibility workshop and an in-depth SRE/infra deep dive week of Apr 6.
topics: Air-gapped deployment flow and offline updates
Key management (HSM/KMS) and encryption at rest/in transit

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-30
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendes (Redwood), Michael Anders (Aurion CTO), Sara Kim (Head of MLOps), Lee Park (Infra), Daniel Ortiz (Security)

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh this is Jordan with Redwood. we got Priya and Carlos from the infra team here, can folks introduce quickly?
[00:08] Michael Anders: Michael Anders, CTO at Aurion, hi.
[00:11] Sara Kim: Sara, MLOps.
[00:13] Lee Park: Lee, infra manager.
[00:15] Daniel Ortiz: Daniel, security.
[00:18] Priya Patel: Hi all, quick agenda — understand your constraints for air-gapped onprem, talk about our Private deployment model and offline update story, then next steps for pilot.
[00:28] Michael Anders: Great, high level we are a manufacturing biz, heavy IP, a lot of PII in change logs, and we cannot allow outbound connections from control plane. basically fully air-gapped. we're evaluating options: hosted is out, dedicated maybe, but private onprem airgapped is what we need.
[00:45] Jordan Lee: Understood — thanks. can you run through your current infra? what hardware you have, and who owns procurement?
[00:52] Sara Kim: we're standardized on internal colos, we have NVIDIA A40 in two racks, some older A100s for training, but the inference clusters are mostly T4 right now. procurement is centralized but we'll likely need a capex request for additional GPUs.
[01:12] Lee Park: and network is isolated, no egress to internet from the production VLANs. we have an internal jump host for controlled updates.
[01:20] Priya Patel: ok that's helpful. two quick clarifications: 1) when you say air-gapped, do you allow physical media transfers (sneakernet) for updates, or do you have an internal repo that gets managed in an isolated way? and 2) what's your update cadence — do you want weekly model updates or quarterly?
[01:36] Michael Anders: we can do signed physical media or we have an internal package mirror behind the firewall. Ideally we'd like to control updates centrally but push windows are strictly limited — monthly for models, emergency patches permitted.
[01:46] Daniel Ortiz: security side — we require HSM-backed key management and full audit trail of requests, plus tamper-evident installer checks. also need to know if Redwood can operate on an air-gapped control plane or if there's any remote telemetry.
[02:00] Carlos Mendes: yes on the HSM support — Redwood Private supports external HSMs via PKCS#11 integrations and we can wire in customer KMS. Priya: do you want to walk through the binary/installer flow?
[02:12] Priya Patel: sure — so our onprem package is a signed installer that can be transferred via physical media. the control plane can be deployed in your VPC with no outbound egress. for updates we provide a signed update bundle; customers verify the signature with their own root of trust — that's why HSM or offline signing is key.
[02:28] Michael Anders: that's promising. how are model weights managed? do weights leave the air-gapped network during packaging?
[02:35] Priya Patel: weights are packaged inside the signed bundle. the packaging can be done inside your environment — in practice we provide a build tool that runs inside the customer's network (no outbound). for customers who cannot run that, Redwood can perform offline packaging on a sealed environment and provide the signed bundle on encrypted media.
[02:52] Sara Kim: do you support quantized models? our edge folks want int8 to save memory and cost.
[02:58] Carlos Mendes: yes, our runtime supports quantization profiles and we can bake quantized variants for inference. however, there are trade-offs with accuracy that we typically include in the rollout plan.
[03:10] Lee Park: what about runtime dependencies and CVEs — we patch OS and libs. what's the maintenance story?
[03:17] Priya Patel: maintenance can be handled two ways: customer-managed updates (you run the patch/update window) or Redwood-assisted where we prepare the signed bundles and a customer operator performs the installation. for critical CVEs we can supply emergency signed patches to be installed via the same offline flow.
[03:30] Daniel Ortiz: auditability is key — retention of logs for 7 years, and ability to export chain of custody for model updates. can you confirm you ship audit logs in a tamper-evident format?
[03:43] Jordan Lee: we produce structured audit logs with integrity checks; for Private deployments we can export logs to a customer-owned syslog or S3-compatible onprem store. we also timestamp and sign critical events.
[03:53] Michael Anders: latency is a concern too — our inference endpoints need <50ms p95 for short prompts in some factories. can you meet that on T4s or do we need A100s?
[04:05] Carlos Mendes: depends on model and batching. for smaller Llama-style models on T4 you can hit that p95 for short context if you keep batch sizes low and enable KV caching. for larger models or high concurrency A100s or H100s are recommended. we'll include tested performance numbers in the hardware spec we send.
[04:28] Sara Kim: cost tradeoffs — we have a capex and opex model. what does Redwood recommend for cost control — batching, quantization, or something else?
[04:36] Priya Patel: batching and caching are the big levers. quantization reduces memory and can lower hardware needs. also model routing — use smaller models for high QPS paths, and fall back to larger models only when needed. Redwood Optimize gives recommendations based on traces.
[04:51] Michael Anders: procurement will ask about support SLAs — can you do 24/7 on-call with a dedicated engineering channel?
[04:59] Jordan Lee: yes, for Private deployments we have enterprise tiers that include 24/7 support and an assigned TAM. that is part of the Dedicated/Private contract.
[05:08] Daniel Ortiz: legal will require indemnity language and we have to review your supply chain for third-party libs. do you provide SBOMs?
[05:14] Carlos Mendes: yes we provide SBOMs for our distro and the runtime components; the air-gapped installer includes SBOM artifacts.
[05:21] Lee Park: on the ops side, can we run Redwood alongside our existing prom stack? we want metrics exported to our prometheus and traces to Jaeger internally.
[05:30] Priya Patel: yes, we export Prom-compatible metrics and have tracing hooks. all telemetry can be pointed to onprem collectors.
[05:36] Michael Anders: timelines — we're aiming to pick a vendor by end of Q2, pilot in Q3, and limited production Q4. procurement needs cost estimates for capex this month.
[05:48] Jordan Lee: understood — we'll prioritize sending the hardware spec + capex estimate and the security pack this week.
[05:56] Sara Kim: wanted to raise one more thing — offline model validation. we need a way to run model evals inside the air-gapped network and reproduce Redwood's evals. is that supported?
[06:06] Priya Patel: yes we supply an evaluation harness that can run in your environment; we provide dataset templates and scripts. results are local but we can guide interpretation. the harness runs with no external calls.
[06:18] Michael Anders: ok sounds good. any blockers with licensing? we prefer a perpetual on-prem runtime license plus a subscription for updates/support.
[06:27] Jordan Lee: that licensing model is supported — perpetual runtime with annual support/updates is an option. we'll document pricing.
[06:35] Daniel Ortiz: last question — how do you verify the integrity of the model weights through the chain?
[06:40] Carlos Mendes: we compute signed checksums for bundles and include a manifest signed with the vendor key; customers can verify with their root of trust. HSM can be used to store the verification keys.
[06:50] Priya Patel: recap — Redwood Private supports fully air-gapped deployments via signed installers and offline update bundles, HSM/KMS integration, SBOMs, Prom metrics onprem, and optional Redwood-assisted packaging.
[07:02] Jordan Lee: next steps are the action items we mentioned. we'll send the SOC2 and security pack, hardware spec, and schedule the feasibility workshop.
[07:12] Michael Anders: thanks all, that sounds useful. we'll review and get procurement aligned.
[07:18] Sara Kim: thanks, bye.

Transcript notes: occasional transcription errors: 'key-value cache' transcribed as 'key-value cash' in some segments, 'HSM' sometimes recognized as 'ash em'. also speaker labels may be mapped to generic 'Speaker 1' in a few timestamps in the raw export.
